reader.requirement: At --std 85 every data description entry in the Report Section must begin with a level-number (01-49, one or two digits); an entry that begins with a clause or with a data-name is refused.
reader.edition-search: reportGroupEntry is `levelNumber (dataName)? reportGroupBody DOT` with no predicate on the level-number; grep of CobolReportWriter.g4 and CobolData.g4#levelNumber for edition predicates found none on the level-number; the only edition-dependent predicate on the entry (entryNameHere) sits on the optional name after it.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf09_07 covers a COLUMN entry with no level-number; not an entry beginning with a data-name, nor single-digit level-numbers in the Report Section

probes.expected: refused: a data-name written before the level-number

citations.check: OK  §1985:XIII.3.14.3 SR1  (3.14.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1

reader.notes: The requirement is structural: the grammar has no report-entry production without levelNumber, so any entry lacking one is a parse error. The refusal is the generic COBOL0001 rather than a named diagnostic; it is correct but not specific.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85, refusal forms the reader did not try: rlv2.cob the FIRST entry after RD written as 'TYPE IS DETAIL.' with no level-number: COBOL0001 unexpected 'TYPE'; rlv3.cob a printable item written 'COLUMN 3 PIC X(2) VALUE ...' under a 05 line entry: COBOL0001 unexpected 'COLUMN'; rlv1.cob '005 LINE PLUS 1' (three digits, not a level-number in the 1985 sense of one or two digits): COBOL1746. The grammar CobolReportWriter.g4#reportGroupEntry has no alternative without levelNumber and no edition predicate on it, so the rule is enforced the same at every edition, which matches the 1985 text. cite.py: OK  §1985:XIII.3.14.3 SR1  (3.14.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1.
